candidates.exact_span: Reporting periods shall end on the last day of each month.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines the monthly monitoring period boundaries used to evaluate whether monitoring was required and reported for each month in Federal FY2025; different interpretation of period boundaries could change which months are in scope and how missing end-of-period data is classified.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee is required to submit regular monthly reports no later than the 15th day of the month.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes a recurring monthly reporting deadline; interpretation of which calendar month the 15th refers to (e.g., the month following the reporting period) could change whether submitted evidence is timely and whether monitoring obligations for a given period are satisfied.

candidates.exact_span: The annual sludge report required in Part IV of the permit is due on February 19 of each year and covers the previous calendar year from January 1 through December 31.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Creates a distinct annual sludge monitoring/reporting obligation with a calendar-year coverage window; interpretation affects whether sludge monitoring was required during FY2025 and how absent sludge reports are classified under missing-evidence semantics.

candidates.exact_span: If any 30 day average, monthly average, 7 day average, weekly average, or daily maximum value exceeds the effluent limitations specified in Part I.A, the permittee shall report the excursion in accordance with the requirements of Part III.D.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Specifies which statistical forms (30-day, monthly, 7-day, weekly, daily maximum) are compared against Part I.A effluent limitations; different interpretation of which average type applies to a given parameter/limit could change the applicable limit comparison (A) and whether excursion reporting was triggered (B).

candidates.exact_span: Any 30 day average, monthly average, 7 day average, weekly average, or daily maximum value reported in the required Discharge Monitoring Report which is in excess of the effluent limitation specified in Part I.A shall constitute evidence of violation of such effluent limitation and of this permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Ties exceedance findings to specific reported statistic types on required DMRs; interpretation of which statistic form governs a given limit affects limit-exceedance evaluation (A), and the limitation to reported values affects how unreported or missing measurements are distinguished from established violations (C).

candidates.exact_span: Other measurements of oxygen demand (e.g., TOC and COD) may be substituted for five day Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD5) or for five day Carbonaceous Biochemical Oxygen Demand (CBOD5), as applicable, where the permittee can demonstrate long term correlation of the method with BOD5 or CBOD5 values, as applicable. Details of the correlation procedures used must be submitted and prior approval granted by the permitting authority for this procedure to be acceptable. Data reported must also include evidence to show that the proper correlation continues to exist after approval.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Governs whether substitute oxygen-demand parameters may stand in for BOD5/CBOD5 limits; interpretation of correlation demonstration, prior approval, and ongoing correlation evidence could change which numeric limit applies to reported values (A), whether substitute monitoring satisfies monitoring obligations (B), and the evidence state when substitute data are present without documented approval (C).

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall report all overflows with the Discharge Monitoring Report submittal.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes overflow reporting as a required element of DMR submittals; interpretation affects whether overflow monitoring/reporting was obligatory and how periods without overflow documentation are classified under missing-evidence semantics.

candidates.exact_span: These reports shall be summarized and reported in tabular format. The summaries shall include: the date, time, duration, location, estimated volume, and cause of the overflow; observed environmental impacts from the overflow; actions taken to address the overflow; and ultimate discharge location if not contained (e.g., storm sewer system, ditch, tributary).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Specifies required overflow report content; interpretation of which fields must be present could change whether submitted overflow evidence satisfies the monitoring/reporting obligation.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall report any noncompliance which may endanger health or the environment.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Creates a conditional immediate-reporting obligation tied to noncompliance that may endanger health or the environment; interpretation of what circumstances qualify could change whether this reporting requirement was applicable during FY2025.
